doc.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1960-09-03

title: The Creole 'legged sisters' and actor Ernest Whitman
summary: Boote describes pretty Creole sisters from New Orleans, one married to actor Ernest Whitman, and says the Whitman sisters were Creole too.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Now, they had three legged sisters. One was married to Honest Whitman, you know, just to be, what did he play with Ethel Waters, Bill. They were from here, the legged sisters. They were popular show people that were married. One was married to Ernest Whitman.

Bill, with Ethel Waters, that series that they had on the radio. Oh, yeah, he was an actor. Yeah. And Hattie McDaniel, he used to play with her. Well, he was married to one of the legged sisters from him. They had quite a few Louisiana, nice actresses, and actresses. And their names
Yeah, their name was legged sisters.
I don't know one name, I know one's name, Melina. I don't forget all their names. It's been quite a long time ago.
were pretty Creole girls. Very pretty girls.
Creole girls. So was, I don't know
Whitman sisters were Creole, but they were beautiful women too, Whitman sisters.
